objective: Choose a sufficient model and effort for first-pass completion, then reduce total time and usage including rework. Expected labels are research-informed hypotheses, not execution results.

sources.title: OpenAI model catalog
sources.claim: Astra is positioned for the most demanding work; Sol is a flagship, Terra balances intelligence and cost, Luna targets cost-sensitive workloads.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra model
sources.claim: Astra supports low, medium, high, xhigh and max; standard API input/output prices are $10/$50 per million tokens.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Sol model
sources.claim: Sol is a flagship GPT-5.6 model; standard API input/output prices are $4/$20 per million tokens.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Terra model
sources.claim: Terra approximately corresponds to the earlier mini tier; standard API input/output prices are $2/$12 per million tokens.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Luna model
sources.claim: Luna approximately corresponds to the earlier nano tier; standard API input/output prices are $0.20/$1.20 per million tokens.

sources.title: Reasoning models
sources.claim: Effort guides deliberation; lower effort generally favors speed and token economy; models adapt reasoning to tasks. Effort levels are not outcome guarantees.

sources.title: Choosing between Astra, Sol, Terra and Luna
sources.claim: Luna suits clear repeatable tasks, Terra everyday judgment, Sol complex open-ended work, Astra hardest end-to-end work. Use the lowest sufficient effort; levels have no exact equivalence across generations.

sources.title: ChatGPT Work and Codex pricing
sources.claim: Usage varies with model, task, context, reasoning, tools, retrieval and caching. Local/cloud work share allowance and weekly limits may apply. Published five-hour ranges are estimates, not fixed limits or weekly conversion factors.

sources.title: Using GPT-6 Astra
sources.claim: Astra can use fewer output tokens on some evaluations despite higher per-token pricing; a larger model is not necessarily more expensive per completed task.

provenance.source: Read-only thread Review TPO findings files (01a0bce8-824b-7f13-9fcd-21063d66d285), preview and recent user message, 2026-09-20.

cases.prompt: Catch up on the dirty files describing the review findings and my work so far. Let me know once you are done.

context.originalTask: Local review tracker documents describe completed, deferred and still-open findings. Inspect Git status and the relevant documents; summarize the current state without implementing or publishing.

expected.rationale: Reading several potentially inconsistent progress documents requires synthesis, but does not yet require solving every underlying code issue.

provenance.source: Read-only thread Verify Forminator pro field OGs (01a0a996-4397-7a52-838d-d4dacf303533), user message, read 2026-09-20.

cases.prompt: Verify that forms with no Pro fields never show Pro field option groups.

context.originalTask: Investigate the existing Forminator/Divi issue with source and permitted focused verification. Existing explanation is unproven; compare field metadata, filtering and UI visibility across relevant form types.

expected.rationale: Establishing a negative claim across metadata and UI states is integration diagnosis, despite the concise prompt.

provenance.source: Synthetic controlled case authored for routing evaluation; not a past user request.

cases.prompt: What was the last commit I made here before the broken migration, across the rebased branch and detached recovery worktree?

context.originalTask: Two identities, rewritten history and a detached recovery tree are present. The user wants attribution and ordering evidence, not merely HEAD. Do not modify refs.

expected.rationale: Similar wording to the simple commit question now requires reconstructing history and resolving ambiguity.
